samples.summary: Gate 1b re-reads (pins) the head SHA but never re-reads the base ref — a base retarget landing between the base check and the file listing empties the list and the gate passes
samples.evidence: `ranBaseCiDefinition` reads `pr.baseRefName` from the snapshot taken at line 137-143 and compares it to `defaultBranch()` (line 231-237), then fetches `pulls/N/files` (line 239), then re-reads `headRefOid` (line 246) explicitly "so it covers the whole window in which the evidence was gathered". But `pulls/N/files` is computed by GitHub against the PR's base AT REQUEST TIME, and the base is never re-read. An author who flips the base from `main` to a branch that already carries the gutted CI definition after line 232 but before line 239 gets an empty/clean file list, the head-pin at line 246 still matches (no push happened), and gate 1b returns true. The gate's own comment (a) says the base is author-controlled and mutable, which is exactly why it is checked — yet the mutable-field pinning treatment given to the head is not given to the base. Fix: re-read `baseRefName` alongside `headRefOid` after the file listing.

samples.summary: Off-by-one in the file-list page bound: a PR with exactly 1000 changed files is refused, contradicting the comment that says it must not be
samples.evidence: Lines 195-197 state: "`<=` and 100-per-page: 10 full pages is 1000 files enumerated, so the throw below is reached only by a PR with MORE than that — an off-by-one here would refuse a PR with exactly 1000." The loop only returns early via `if (files.length < 100) return hits;` (line 211). For exactly 1000 files, page 10 returns 100 (not < 100), the loop exits and line 213 throws `more than 1000 changed files`, so `ranBaseCiDefinition` returns false and the PR is refused — precisely the behaviour the comment says would be a bug. (mark-ready.test.mjs's `atTheBound` case asserts this refusal, so the code and the comment disagree about intent.) Impact is a fail-closed refusal of a legal 1000-file PR, so it is contained, but either the comment or the bound is wrong.

samples.summary: `ciRunToRerun` can select a run that is not the run gate 1 reads, producing a panel round that can never promote and no further admissible panel event
samples.evidence: `ciRunToRerun` returns the newest COMPLETED run, while `ciConclusion` (gate 1, mark-ready.mjs:178) returns the newest run by id regardless of status, and the panel's `ci` job (agent-review-panel.yml:300-336) reads the TRIGGERING run. When a head SHA carries two runs (close/reopen files a second `pull_request` run — the docstring at checks.mjs:165-170 acknowledges this) and the newer one is still in flight, `@claude rerun` re-runs the older finished run. That emits `completed` with `run_attempt > 1`, which the panel gate admits; the panel's `ci` job sees that run succeed and promote runs; but mark-ready's gate 1 reads the NEWER (in-flight) run, gets `null`, and exits 1 ("leaving as draft"). The newer run's own `completed` event arrives with `run_attempt == 1` and is REFUSED by the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:168-169), so no further panel round is admitted and the PR sits as a draft — the exact failure mode the comment at agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1461 exists to prevent. The docstring's claim that "gate 1 reads whichever ends up newest when it next runs" assumes a next panel round that the gate does not admit.

samples.summary: The inline mirrors of `ciRunToRerun` drop the `?? 0` id fallback that checks.mjs uses, so the copies disagree on runs with a missing/undefined `id`
samples.evidence: checks.mjs:202 uses `((r.id ?? 0) > (newest.id ?? 0) ? r : newest)`; the mirrors in agent-loop.yml:160 and agent-rerun.yml:204 use `(n === null || r.id > n.id ? r : n)`. With `id` undefined, `undefined > undefined` is false so the mirror keeps the first element, while `newestRun` compares 0 > 0 and also keeps the first — equal here, but a mixed list (one run with an id, one without) diverges: checks.mjs picks the one with an id, the mirror keeps whichever came first. The pinning test in checks.test.mjs only uses fixtures where every run has an `id`, so the divergence is unpinned. Defensive only — the API always returns `id`.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: in ranBaseCiDefinition (mark-ready.mjs:224-270) the base is read once from the line 137-143 snapshot and compared to defaultBranch() at 231-237, then pulls/N/files is fetched at 239 (via ciDefiningPathsChanged, mark-ready.mjs:199) — an endpoint evaluated against the PR's base at request time — and only headRefOid is re-read afterwards (line 246, a --json list containing that single field, compared at 247). A base retarget landing in that window is undetectable, since retargeting does not change headRefOid. I searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide grep for baseRefName/base_ref/default_branch/defaultBranch shows the only other reads are the initial snapshot (142), the test fixture plumbing (mark-ready.test.mjs:80,121,416-434) and unrelated eval/extract-corpus.mjs; the sole caller (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1494-1548, gated at 1463-1465) performs no base check; gate 1 (ciPassed, 159-179) and checks.mjs::ciConclusion (193-197) inspect nothing base-related; the promote path re-reads only labels (360). The design doc confirms the asymmetry as-built (harness-engineering.md:1952-1961: base refused up front, head "re-read after the enumeration"), and the trusted baseline (.trusted/.../mark-ready.mjs:108) does not fetch baseRefName at all, so no prior implementation supplies the missing re-read. In-lane for correctness as an ordering/TOCTOU gap that breaks the invariant the code itself asserts at lines 34-43 ("pinned twice ... both are mutable"), leaving a fail-closed gate able to pass on a file list gathered against a different base than the one it validated.

verdict.reason: Every cited fact checks out. `ciRunToRerun` (checks.mjs:231-233) selects the newest COMPLETED run while `ciConclusion` (checks.mjs:193-203), which gate 1 uses (mark-ready.mjs:178), takes the newest run by id and returns null when it is in flight; the panel's `ci` job polls only the TRIGGERING run (agent-review-panel.yml:300-313), so a re-run of the older finished run can report success while gate 1 reads the newer unfinished run and exits 1 with the benign "leaving as draft" path (agent-review-panel.yml:1531-1542) and no page. The premise is reachable: ci.yml:9-10 uses `pull_request` with default types (includes `reopened`), so one SHA can carry two runs, and the docstring at checks.mjs:165-170/213-219 concedes both the two-run case and the divergence. I searched for a closing guard and found none: the newer run's `requested` round shares the `active` concurrency group (agent-review-panel.yml:115-118, cancel-in-progress: true) with the rerun round and is cancelled silently (cancelled rounds do not page, per the note at 100-103), and its later `completed`/attempt-1 event is refused by the gate at agent-review-panel.yml:164-169. Result: a stuck draft recoverable only by another human rerun — the exact mode the comment at 1454-1461 exists to prevent. The window is narrow (requires the newer run to still be in flight when promote evaluates), which bears on severity, not on whether the defect exists; no named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Gate 1b reads the PR's diff against its OWN base branch, so a PR stacked on a branch that already gutted the CI definition passes the gate
finding.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` calls `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${number}/files`, which enumerates the diff of head against the PULL REQUEST'S BASE, not against `main`. The gate's stated invariant (mark-ready.mjs:20-29, and the report line at :238 "CI ran main's definition") only holds when base IS the default branch, and nothing in this script or in the promote job checks that: `pr view --json` at :122-128 never fetches `baseRefName`, and grep of scripts/agent finds no base-branch constraint anywhere on the promote path. Concretely: branch A edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to remove every test (PR A is refused by 1b, as intended, and just sits there); branch B is opened with base=A and contains only code. `pulls/B/files` returns no `.github/workflows/**` entry, `branchEditsCiDefinition` returns false, gate 1b passes — while B's `pull_request` CI run executed the merge ref of A+B, i.e. exactly the gutted ci.yml the gate exists to refuse. The panel itself does not share this blind spot (agent-review-panel.yml:455 diffs against `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`), so the two halves of the pipeline disagree about what "the branch changed" means, and 1b is the permissive one.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. There is no `branchEditsCiDefinition`; gate 1b is `ranBaseCiDefinition` (mark-ready.mjs:224). The claim that `baseRefName` is never fetched is false — it is in the `pr view --json` field list at mark-ready.mjs:142. The claim that no base-branch constraint exists is false — `ranBaseCiDefinition` reads the repo's `default_branch` via `defaultBranch()` (mark-ready.mjs:216-222) and throws if `pr.baseRefName !== base` (mark-ready.mjs:232-237), BEFORE calling `ciDefiningPathsChanged` (mark-ready.mjs:239). The throw is caught and returns false (fail-closed, mark-ready.mjs:262-269), and `ciDefinitionGate` must be true for promotion (mark-ready.mjs:272, 300, 313-318). The finding's concrete scenario (PR B based on branch A) is therefore refused at the base check, never measured. The comment at mark-ready.mjs:226-230 names this exact stacked-PR case, and the head-SHA re-pin at mark-ready.mjs:246-252 closes the companion race. The finding describes an earlier revision, not the working tree.
